# ISA — Ideal State Artifact

The ISA is the single document that articulates "done" for any thing whose ideal state we are pursuing — a project, an application, a library, infrastructure, a work session, an art piece, a strategic decision. It serves five identities simultaneously: ideal state articulation, test harness, build verification, done condition, system of record.

This skill owns the canonical template, the workflows that generate and refine ISAs, and the example library.

---

## The Twelve-Section Body (locked v6.2.0)

Every ISA may have up to twelve body sections. The tier completeness gate decides which are required at which effort tier; sections never appear empty. **Order is fixed**.

| # | Section | Purpose | Written At |
|---|---------|---------|------------|
| 1 | `## Problem` | What is broken or missing right now that makes the ideal state worth pursuing | OBSERVE |
| 2 | `## Vision` | What euphoric surprise looks like — experiential intent, 1–5 sentences | OBSERVE |
| 3 | `## Out of Scope` | Anti-vision — what is *not* included in this ideal state, declared upfront in prose | OBSERVE |
| 4 | `## Principles` | Substrate-independent truths (Deutsch reach) the work must respect | OBSERVE |
| 5 | `## Constraints` | Immovable architectural mandates that bound the solution space | OBSERVE |
| 6 | `## Goal` | The hard-to-vary spine — 1–3 sentences naming verifiable done | OBSERVE |
| 7 | `## Criteria` | Atomic ISCs (Ideal State Criteria) — one binary tool probe each, including derived `Anti:` ISCs | OBSERVE → EXECUTE |
| 8 | `## Test Strategy` | Per-ISC verification approach — `isc | type | check | threshold | tool` | OBSERVE/PLAN |
| 9 | `## Features` | Work breakdown — `name | description | satisfies: [ISC-N…] | depends_on: [feature…] | parallelizable: bool` | PLAN |
| 10 | `## Decisions` | Timestamped decision log including dead ends; `refined:` prefix for Goal/ISC restructures | any phase |
| 11 | `## Changelog` | Conjecture / refuted-by / learned / criterion-now entries — Deutsch error-correction trail | LEARN |
| 12 | `## Verification` | Evidence that each ISC passed — quoted command output, file content, screenshot path | VERIFY |

---

## Three-Guardrail Taxonomy (Principles vs Constraints vs Anti-criteria)

Adjacent concepts. Distinguished by **who they bind**.

| Guardrail | Binds | Tone | Example | Lives In |
|-----------|-------|------|---------|----------|
| **Principles** | The *thinking* | Aspirational, generalizable | "User-facing systems prioritize responsiveness." | `## Principles` |
| **Constraints** | The *solution space* | Immovable, non-negotiable | "We do not roll our own cryptography — OAuth via industry-standard libraries only." | `## Constraints` |
| **Out of Scope** | The *vision* | Declared, explicit, prose | "Mobile native apps are not part of v1." | `## Out of Scope` |
| **Anti-criteria** | The *test surface* | Granular, testable, yes/no | "Anti: /admin returns 200 in v1 build." | `## Criteria` (with `Anti:` prefix) |

The first three are author-stated (declarative). Anti-criteria are derived — they are how Out of Scope, Constraints, and Principles become probe-able.

---

## Tier Completeness Gate (HARD at all tiers)

Mirrors the v6.1.0 thinking-floor non-relaxability. Required sections per tier:

| Tier | Required Sections |
|------|-------------------|
| **E1** | Goal, Criteria |
| **E2** | Problem, Goal, Criteria, Test Strategy |
| **E3** | Problem, Vision, Out of Scope, Constraints, Goal, Criteria, Features, Test Strategy |
| **E4** | All twelve sections |
| **E5** | All twelve + active Interview workflow run before BUILD |

**Project ISA override:** any `<project>/ISA.md` requires E3+ structure regardless of the active task's tier. The project file is the long-lived source of truth; one transient E1 task must not downgrade it.

`CheckCompleteness` workflow enforces this gate. A miss blocks `phase: complete` until the missing sections are filled in.

---

## Workflow Routing

Match the verb in the request to a workflow. When ambiguous, default to Scaffold for new ISAs and CheckCompleteness for audits.

| Verb / Intent | Workflow | File |
|---------------|----------|------|
| "scaffold", "create", "generate", "new ISA from this prompt", "extract feature as ephemeral" | **Scaffold** | `Workflows/Scaffold.md` |
| "interview me", "fill in the ISA", "deepen", "ask me questions" | **Interview** | `Workflows/Interview.md` |
| "check", "audit", "score this ISA", "is it complete?" | **CheckCompleteness** | `Workflows/CheckCompleteness.md` |
| "reconcile", "merge feature file back", "ephemeral → master" | **Reconcile** | `Workflows/Reconcile.md` |
| "seed", "bootstrap from this repo", "draft an ISA from existing code" | **Seed** | `Workflows/Seed.md` |
| "append decision", "append changelog", "append verification", "record C/R/L entry" | **Append** | `Workflows/Append.md` |

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **ISA** skill to ACTION...
```

---

## Gotchas

The highest-information-density part of this skill. Each entry captures a non-obvious failure mode that has bitten real ISA work.

- **ID-stability is the cornerstone of Reconcile — never re-number on edit.** When the Splitting Test produces a finer-grained version of `ISC-7`, preserve `ISC-7` as the parent and add `ISC-7.1`, `ISC-7.2`, etc. Even when an ISC is dropped, leave a tombstone (`- [ ] ISC-N: [DROPPED — see Decisions YYYY-MM-DD]`). Reconcile keys on stable IDs; renumbering breaks ephemeral feature-file merges silently and the failure mode looks like "the worker's checkmarks didn't land in master."
- **Ephemeral files are derived views, never sources of truth.** Scaffold's `--ephemeral` mode produces a slice of the master ISA at `MEMORY/WORK/{slug}/_ephemeral/<feature>.md`. Workers operate against that slice; Reconcile merges back. Hand-editing master content from an ephemeral file is policy-forbidden — the master is what persists; the ephemeral is what gets archived.
- **The Changelog format is non-negotiable.** Every entry needs all four pieces (`conjectured`, `refuted by`, `learned`, `criterion now`) in that order. **Not ready to answer yet. The findings are plausible, but several load-bearing points are unverified and the framing may miss Nick's actual scenario.**

**Checks that could change the verdict**

1. **Generic resend action.** The checkout is on `fix/audit-log-resend-and-email-noise`, and PR #102 adds a "resend" audit label, so some admin resend exists. Establish exactly which emails it can resend before saying there is no admin resend of a payment link. If it resends the submission or exemption-rejected email, and that carries the pay link, part 2 becomes "partly, by a workaround".

2. **The ordinary unpaid case.** A priced request lands in AWAITING_PAYMENT at submission, so "did not pay" may already be that state with nothing to mark. Confirm three things:
   - **Intent creation:** whether the PaymentIntent is created at submit or only when the member reaches the pay step. If it is lazy, the pay page may not work for an abandoned request.
   - **Missing intent:** whether `/pay/id` creates an intent when none exists, or errors.
   - **Way back:** whether the submission confirmation email or member portal has a pay link.
   
   If the page works, the practical answer may be that the admin can copy the URL by hand today.

3. **Requests that skipped payment.** This is the other reading of Nick's question. Check for an admin-created or on-behalf request path, a price added after submission, and an exemption approved in error. Confirm no transition leads back to AWAITING_PAYMENT from AWAITING_APPROVAL or later. Also check whether SUBMITTED is ever a persisted resting state; if not, PAYMENT_REQUIRED is dead code and you should say so.

4. **Pay page and webhook guards.** Check whether `/pay/id` checks that the status is AWAITING_PAYMENT, and whether it is unauthenticated or tokenised. Check whether the webhook transitions only from AWAITING_PAYMENT. If it is unguarded, a payment on a request in another state could move it wrongly or do nothing; either is worth reporting.

5. **Reminder template has no link.** Read both the HTML and text variants and any shared layout or CTA component. A link is often injected by a wrapper, not the template body. Also check whether the reminder fires once or repeats.

**ISCs your summary leaves open**

- **ISC-27 (origin/main parity):** not mentioned. Run `git grep` on `origin/main` for the transition map, webhook, cron and pay route.
- **Empty `confirm-payment` directory:** git does not track empty directories, so this is a local artefact. Run `git log --all -- <path>` to see whether a route existed, was deleted, or lives on another branch. Do not present it as evidence about production.

- **ISC-28 (backlog docs):** check `context/state.md` and the project ISA for a known payment-required item.

**Caveats to carry into the answer**

- **Cron:** code presence does not mean it runs. Scheduler config has known Terraform drift and a `cron_secret` mismatch. Say "the code has a daily reminder" and do not claim members receive it.
- **Terminology:** the ISA says "checkout session" but the code uses PaymentIntents. Use the code's terms.
- **Scope:** this is advice only. Give a verdict for each of the three parts and name the gaps. Do not propose or start a build.

**Likely verdict if the checks hold**

- **Mark as payment required:** no manual admin action; the state is automatic at submission or on exemption rejection.
- **Send a payment link:** no dedicated admin action; a pay page exists and the link is only emailed on exemption rejection.
- **Status update on payment:** yes, via the webhook to AWAITING_APPROVAL.

---
task: "Build require-payment, resend-link, abandoned sweep, member cancel link"
slug: 20261010-accessbuddy-require-payment-build
project: accessbuddy
effort: advanced
effort_source: classifier
phase: observe
progress: 0/36
mode: interactive
started: 2026-10-10T09:00:00+11:00
updated: 2026-10-10T09:00:00+11:00

## Problem

AccessBuddy has no admin action to demand payment on a request, no way to resend a payment link, and a member who abandons the Stripe step leaves the request in SUBMITTED where no queue column renders it and no reminder targets it. The only email that carries a pay link is the exemption-rejected email. Members have no cancel path from an email.

## Vision

An approver opens any unpaid request and sees "Require payment" or "Resend payment link". The member gets a branded email with a Pay button and a "Cancel this request" link that works without signing in. Overnight, abandoned requests move themselves to Awaiting Payment and the member is emailed. Nothing silently sits in SUBMITTED again.

## Out of Scope

No manual "record offline payment" action. No change to Stripe account model or webhooks beyond intent cancellation hygiene. No migration (the cancel link is a signed token, not a stored column). No deploy; this ships as a PR for Nick to merge.

## Constraints

- Branch from origin/main; PR #102 branch untouched.
- Postgres RLS: writes go through withTenant; cron selects follow the existing bare-db pattern.
- Email rendering goes through sendTemplatedEmail so setEmailBranding runs.
- No new env vars; cancel token signs with the existing SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET.
- bun only; TypeScript only; Australian English in copy.
- Commit prefix feat: so release-please ships it on merge.

## Goal

A PR on branch feat/require-payment-and-abandoned-sweep that adds the PAYMENT_REQUIRED transition with intent creation and email, an admin resend-payment-link action, a nightly abandoned-payment sweep, and a signed cancel link on the pay page, with typecheck and tests green.

## Criteria

- [ ] ISC-1: state-machine.ts allows PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL as well as SUBMITTED
- [ ] ISC-2: requests.ts resolveNewStatus maps PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL to AWAITING_PAYMENT
- [ ] ISC-3: shared state-machine test covers PAYMENT_REQUIRED from both states and rejects it from AWAITING_PROGRAMMING
- [ ] ISC-4: transitionRequest creates a Stripe intent on PAYMENT_REQUIRED when none exists
- [ ] ISC-5: transitionRequest persists paymentAmountCents and paymentExempt=false on PAYMENT_REQUIRED
- [ ] ISC-6: transitionRequest sends the paymentRequired email on PAYMENT_REQUIRED with pay and cancel links
- [ ] ISC-7: new route requests/[id]/payment-required exists, POST, permission APPROVE_EXEMPTION, body {reason}
- [ ] ISC-8: payment-required route refuses paid requests and orphaned requests with a 400
- [ ] ISC-9: new route requests/[id]/resend-payment-link exists, POST, permission APPROVE_EXEMPTION
- [ ] ISC-10: resend route accepts SUBMITTED and AWAITING_PAYMENT only, refuses when paidAt set
- [ ] ISC-11: resend route ensures an intent exists before emailing
- [ ] ISC-12: resend route writes an audit UPDATE entry with metadata.action payment_link_resent
- [ ] ISC-13: shared helper builds paymentUrl and cancelUrl from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, slug, request id
- [ ] ISC-14: cancel token is HMAC-SHA256 over tenantId, requestId, expiry using SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET
- [ ] ISC-15: cancel token verify rejects tampered signature, wrong request id, and expired token (unit test)
- [ ] ISC-16: new public route requests/[id]/cancel-by-token POST {token, reason} transitions CANCEL when valid
- [ ] ISC-17: cancel-by-token refuses paid requests and non-cancellable statuses
- [ ] ISC-18: pay page shows a "Cancel this request" section only when ?cancel=<token> is present
- [ ] ISC-19: pay page cancel posts to cancel-by-token and renders a cancelled confirmation
- [ ] ISC-20: payment-info returns a cancelled flag (no client secret) for cancelled or rejected requests
- [ ] ISC-21: CANCEL on an unpaid request with an intent cancels the Stripe intent best-effort
- [ ] ISC-22: email-events.ts registers payment_required with amount, paymentUrl, cancelUrl variables
- [ ] ISC-23: email-templates.ts paymentRequiredEmail renders amount, Pay button, cancel link
- [ ] ISC-24: email.ts TemplateVariables and renderTemplate include paymentRequired
- [ ] ISC-25: paymentReminder template accepts paymentUrl and cancelUrl and renders both when given
- [ ] ISC-26: cron reminder passes paymentUrl and cancelUrl to paymentReminder
- [ ] ISC-27: cron has an abandoned-payment sweep over SUBMITTED, non-orphaned, paymentExempt=false, unpaid, older than grace
- [ ] ISC-28: sweep transitions each via transitionRequest PAYMENT_REQUIRED with metadata.action abandoned_payment_sweep
- [ ] ISC-29: cron results include abandonedPaymentsSwept counter
- [ ] ISC-30: admin-actions.tsx shows Require Payment (reason form) when PAYMENT_REQUIRED is valid and unpaid
- [ ] ISC-31: admin-actions.tsx shows Resend Payment Link for SUBMITTED or AWAITING_PAYMENT unpaid requests with APPROVE_EXEMPTION
- [ ] ISC-32: queue-filter.tsx renders a Submitted (unpaid) section so same-day abandoned requests are visible
- [ ] ISC-33: audit-trail.tsx labels submitted_awaiting_payment, awaiting_approval_awaiting_payment, payment_link_resent, abandoned sweep, member cancel via link
- [ ] ISC-34: payment-exempt route accepts SUBMITTED as well as AWAITING_PAYMENT
- [ ] ISC-35: bun typecheck and bun test pass across the monorepo
- [ ] ISC-36: Anti: no change to webhook signature handling, Stripe account model, or PR #102 branch

## Test Strategy

| isc | type | check | threshold | tool |
|-----|------|-------|-----------|------|
| 1-3 | unit | vitest state-machine | green | bun test |
| 4-6, 21 | code | Read requests.ts hunks | present | Read |
| 7-12, 16-17, 20, 34 | code | Read route files | present | Read |
| 13-15 | unit | vitest cancel-token + links | green | bun test |
| 18-19, 30-32 | code | Read tsx; typecheck | green | tsc |
| 22-26 | unit | vitest renders template with links | green | bun test |
| 27-29 | code | Read cron hunk | present | Read |
| 33 | code | Read audit-trail labels | present | Read |
| 35 | build | turbo typecheck + test | exit 0 | Bash |
| 36 | git | diff --stat excludes webhook route; PR #102 branch sha unchanged | true | Bash |

## Features

| name | description | satisfies | depends_on | parallelizable |
|------|-------------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| transition | PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL, intent + amount + email | 1-6 | none | no |
| links-and-token | payment-links helper, cancel token sign/verify | 13-15 | none | yes |
| emails | payment_required event, template, reminder links | 22-26 | links-and-token | yes |
| admin-routes | payment-required, resend-payment-link, payment-exempt fix | 7-12, 34 | transition, emails | no |
| member-cancel | cancel-by-token route, pay page cancel UI, payment-info flag, intent cancel | 16-21 | links-and-token | no |
| sweep | cron abandoned sweep + reminder links | 26-29 | transition, emails | no |
| admin-ui | buttons, queue section, audit labels | 30-33 | admin-routes | no |
| verify | typecheck, tests, review | 35-36 | all | no |

## Decisions

- 2026-10-10: Cancel link is a signed token (HMAC over tenantId:requestId:exp with SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET), not a stored column. Avoids a migration, matches the existing session-signing pattern, and expires in 30 days.
- 2026-10-10: PAYMENT_REQUIRED allowed from SUBMITTED and AWAITING_APPROVAL only. ON_HOLD resumes to its prior state first; AWAITING_EXEMPTION_REVIEW already has Reject Exemption.
- 2026-10-10: Both admin actions use Permission.APPROVE_EXEMPTION, matching Grant Exemption and Reject Exemption, the existing payment-adjacent actions.
- 2026-10-10: Sweep grace is 1 hour at the 2am run, so anything left overnight is swept; same-day abandonment is covered by the new queue section.
- 2026-10-10: Delegation: Forge unavailable (codex CLI missing on this box). One Claude-family review agent at VERIFY.

97c1003 feat(payments): require payment, resend payment link, abandoned-payment sweep, member cancel link
Shell cwd was reset to /home/nicholas-wood/.claude

1. **Check Stripe before anything that assumes "unpaid".** The sweep, the resend route, payment-required and cancel-by-token all treat `paidAt` null as unpaid. If a webhook is late or failed, the member has paid but `paidAt` is still null. The sweep would then move them to Awaiting Payment and email "please pay", and the cancel link would cancel a paid request with no refund.
   - Retrieve the intent before acting.
   - If its status is `succeeded` or `processing`, skip it and log it for reconciliation.
   - In cancel-by-token, refuse when the intent is `processing` or `succeeded`. Best-effort cancel of the intent doesn't protect money that has already been taken.

2. **The first sweep will email the whole backlog.** At the first 2am run after merge, every old request stuck in SUBMITTED gets a "payment required" email, including ones that are months old.
   - Add a lower bound, e.g. `createdAt > now() - 14 days`.
   - Or ship with a dry-run flag that only logs.
   - Either way, put the expected first-run count in the PR description so Nick knows what will happen.

3. **Keep the token separate from session tokens.** You're reusing `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`, so the signed message needs its own prefix, e.g. `cancel:v1:${tenantId}:${requestId}:${exp}`. Without it, a token signed for one purpose could be accepted for another. Also:
   - `timingSafeEqual` throws if the two buffers differ in length, which a tampered token causes. Check length first and return 400, not 500.
   - The route must check that the token's `tenantId` matches the tenant from the slug or request. Matching the request id alone isn't enough.

**Should fix (small)**

4. **Stripe and email calls inside a DB transaction.** If you create the intent inside `withTenant` and the transaction then rolls back, the intent is left orphaned. Send the email only after commit, never inside the transaction.
   - Pass an idempotency key to `paymentIntents.create`, e.g. `req-${id}-${amount}`, so a double-click can't create two intents.

5. **"Ensure intent exists" has to cover more than a missing intent.** If the existing intent is `canceled`, which is terminal and happens after a cancel, create a new one. If its amount doesn't match `paymentAmountCents` (the price changed), update or replace it.

6. **Sweep robustness.**
   - Wrap each row in its own try/catch so one Stripe error doesn't stop the run.
   - A request whose credential type has no price will throw every night. Log it once and make sure it shows up somewhere.
   - Each `transitionRequest` call needs a proper `withTenant` scope, not the bare db. Your memory notes a latent bare-db RLS risk in cron at the accessbuddy_app cutover, and this adds a second path into it.
   - Check which actor or `userId` the sweep and the public cancel route record. An audit row with a null user can break the FK or the renderer.

7. **Audit labels.** Your memory says a new `metadata.action` needs labels in *both* renderers. ISC-33 only covers `audit-trail.tsx`. Find the other renderer and add the five new labels there too.

8. **Token in the URL.** The pay page loads Stripe.js, so the `?cancel=` token can leak in the Referer header and in analytics. Set `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on that page, or remove the parameter with `history.replaceState` after reading it. Cap the length of `reason`.

**Test coverage**

Most route ISCs are checked by reading the code, not by tests. At minimum, add unit tests for:
- the sweep's where-clause
- cancel-by-token refusing paid requests and wrong-tenant tokens

ISC-36 should still record the PR #102 branch sha before and after.

The rest is fine and the decisions hold up: `APPROVE_EXEMPTION` for both actions, the 1-hour grace plus the queue section for same-day requests, idempotent cancel, and no migration. Note in the PR description that PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL can override an exemption that was already granted.

Those edits touch `requests.ts`, `stripe.ts`, `payment-links.ts` and `cancel-by-token/route.ts`, and they fix real problems in the staged version, so stage them before committing. **Verdict:** nothing breaks tenant isolation or lets anyone forge a cancel token. Findings 1 to 3 are worth fixing before merge because they can leave a member's money taken and never recorded against the request. Finding 4 means the sweep misses most of the requests it was built for.

## Important (80-89)

**1. Two new paths let a priced orphaned request be paid or exempted without being linked to a member (85)**
- **Where:**
  - `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/requests/[id]/resend-payment-link/route.ts:396` and `lib/services/requests.ts:1932` (`sendPaymentLinkEmail`) don't check `isOrphaned`.
  - `admin-actions.tsx:138` (`canResendPaymentLink`) shows the button on orphaned SUBMITTED requests.
  - `payment-exempt/route.ts:74` now accepts SUBMITTED, also without an orphan check. Before this change the route rejected SUBMITTED, so this path didn't exist.
- **Scenario:** an admin opens an orphaned priced request and clicks Resend Payment Link. A Stripe intent is created and the email goes to `orphanEmail`. The member pays, and the webhook moves the request SUBMITTED → AWAITING_APPROVAL with `isOrphaned=true` and `requesterId=null`. The main queue filters on `isOrphaned=false`, so the request drops out of it. `link-member/route.ts` then rewrites `status`, `paymentExempt` and `paymentAmountCents` without checking `paidAt`, putting a paid request back into AWAITING_PAYMENT. Granting an exemption on an orphan has the same effect.
- **Fix:** reject `isOrphaned` in `sendPaymentLinkEmail` and in payment-exempt, the same way `payment-required/route.ts:323` already does. Add `!isOrphaned` to `canResendPaymentLink` and `canRequirePayment` by passing `isOrphaned` into AdminActions.

**2. Admin or member CANCEL keeps the money when Stripe has charged but the webhook hasn't landed (82)**
- **Where:** `lib/stripe.ts:93` returns quietly when the intent is already `succeeded`, and `lib/services/requests.ts:905` swallows any error from the cancel call. The unstaged `requestHasPaymentInFlight` fixes this only for cancel-by-token.
- **Scenario:** the member pays, so the intent is `succeeded`, but `paidAt` is still null. An admin (`cancel` route) or the signed-in member (`member-cancel`) then cancels. `cancelPaymentIntent` sees `succeeded` and returns. The auto-refund branch is keyed on `paidAt`, so it is skipped. The webhook's PAYMENT_RECEIVED on a CANCELLED request then throws and is only logged. The club keeps the money, the request shows unpaid and cancelled, and nothing refunds it.
- **Fix:** have `cancelPaymentIntent` return the intent status. In transitionRequest, either throw on `succeeded`/`processing`, which rolls the cancel back, or run the refund path. Simplest is to call `requestHasPaymentInFlight` inside transitionRequest for every CANCEL and REJECT, not only from cancel-by-token.

**3. Granting an exemption leaves the emailed pay link working, and a payment made after that is lost (80)**
- **Where:** `payment-exempt/route.ts:74`, with the PAYMENT_EXEMPT transition doing nothing to the intent, and `payment-info/route.ts:49`, which only blocks cancelled and rejected requests.
- **Scenario:** the sweep or an admin emails a pay link, then an admin grants an exemption, so the request is in AWAITING_APPROVAL with the intent still live. The member clicks the old email. payment-info still returns a client secret, and the member pays. PAYMENT_RECEIVED isn't valid from AWAITING_APPROVAL, so the webhook throws and the payment is never recorded. The same gap existed before for AWAITING_PAYMENT, but this change now sends pay links proactively and adds SUBMITTED as an exemptable state, which makes it much more reachable.
- **Fix:** cancel the intent on PAYMENT_EXEMPT and APPROVE_EXEMPTION, reusing the CANCEL block. Separately, have payment-info hand out a client secret only when the status is SUBMITTED or AWAITING_PAYMENT.

**4. The sweep skips brand-new-member requests, the main group it was meant to catch (85)**
- **Where:** `apps/web/src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts:501`, the condition `isNotNull(fobRequests.requesterId)`.
- **Scenario:** in `requests/submit/route.ts`, a `new` request from an email with no user account is inserted with `requesterId: null`, `isOrphaned: false`, `orphanEmail` set, and status SUBMITTED with a live intent. That is exactly a first-time applicant who closes the Stripe step, and they are never swept. `sendTransitionEmail` already falls back to `orphanEmail`, so dropping the condition is safe.
- **Fix:** remove `isNotNull(requesterId)` and rely on `isOrphaned = false`. Optionally require `requesterId IS NOT NULL OR orphanEmail IS NOT NULL`.

## Fixed in the working tree, but only if those edits get staged

- **Cancelled intent reused after a reopen (90):**
  - **Where:** the staged `ensurePaymentIntent` returns `true` whenever `stripePaymentIntentId` is set.
  - **Scenario:** cancel voids the intent, the admin reopens, then Require Payment (or Reject Exemption on a reopened damaged replacement) emails a pay link for a cancelled intent, and the member can't pay.
  - **Fix:** the unstaged rewrite creates a fresh intent when the old one is cancelled.
- **Cancel-by-token trusted `paidAt` alone:** the unstaged `requestHasPaymentInFlight` fixes this. The sweep, Require Payment and Resend could also email a member who had already paid; the unstaged `"paid"` return value fixes that.

## Checked and found safe

- **Tenant isolation:** the public routes resolve the tenant from the slug. `transitionRequest` and `sendPaymentLinkEmail` filter on `tenantId`. The pre-check SELECT in cancel-by-token has no tenant filter, but it only runs after a token bound to `tenantId:requestId` has verified, so it can't reach another tenant's request.
- **HMAC token:**
  - Signing: HMAC-SHA256 over `cancel:v1:tenant:request:expiry`.
  - Comparison: the length check runs before `timingSafeEqual`, which is correct.
  - Shared secret: session cookies sign JSON payloads that start with `{`, so the two can't be confused.
  - Replay: a token can be reused until expiry, but it only ever cancels that member's own request and cancelling is idempotent. Acceptable.
  - Operational note: rotating `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` invalidates every outstanding cancel link.
- **Rollback on PAYMENT_REQUIRED with no price:** `withTenant` wraps everything in `db.transaction`. The throw happens before any Stripe call, so the earlier status UPDATE rolls back. The sweep wraps each request in its own try/catch.
- **Connect handling:** intents are direct charges, and retrieve and cancel both pass `stripeAccount`, which matches.
- **Sweep scope:** damaged-fob auto-exempt requests move to AWAITING_EXEMPTION_REVIEW inside the submit transaction, and linked orphans go to AWAITING_PAYMENT, so neither is swept. ON_HOLD and requests with an exemption requested aren't SUBMITTED.
- **REJECT_EXEMPTION refactor:** behaviour is unchanged except that it now saves `paymentAmountCents`. Before, a request with a null amount got a pay page that returned 400, so this is an improvement.
- **Audit labels:** the new overrides run before the generic label map, and their keys are right.

## Lower-confidence notes (below the reporting bar)

- **Old intent left live (~70):** when the unstaged code replaces an intent because the price changed, it doesn't cancel the old one. A member with the old page open can still pay it. The webhook doesn't check that the intent id matches the request's stored id, so `paidAt` gets set while `stripePaymentIntentId` points at the new, unpaid intent, and a later refund would target the wrong intent.
- **Require Payment button on orphans:** the button shows on orphaned requests and the API then rejects them. This is a UI mismatch only, and the fix in finding 1 covers it.</result>

cat > /tmp/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
## Why

Today a request only ever reaches **Awaiting Payment** automatically (exemption rejected, or orphan linked). A member who submits a priced request and closes the browser at the Stripe step leaves the request in **SUBMITTED**, where no queue column renders it and no reminder targets it. There was no admin way to demand payment, no way to resend a payment link, and the reminder email had no link in it. Members had no way to cancel from an email without signing in.

## What

**Admin actions** (both behind `approve_exemption`, like Grant Exemption)
- **Require Payment** (`POST requests/[id]/payment-required`, reason required). Valid from SUBMITTED and AWAITING_APPROVAL. Creates the Stripe PaymentIntent if the request never got one, records the amount, moves to AWAITING_PAYMENT and emails the member a pay link plus a cancel link. Rolls back if the credential type has no price. Note: from AWAITING_APPROVAL this can override an exemption that was already granted.
- **Resend Payment Link** (`POST requests/[id]/resend-payment-link`). No status change; re-emails pay + cancel links for SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT unpaid requests. Audited as `payment_link_resent`.

**Nightly abandoned-payment sweep** (in the existing daily cron)
- SUBMITTED, not orphaned, not exempt, priced, unpaid, older than 1 hour and younger than 30 days → `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` via the normal transition, so the member gets the payment email. Counter `abandonedPaymentsSwept` in the cron result. The 30 day bound stops the first run emailing a stale backlog; older ones show in the new **Submitted (unpaid)** queue section for manual action.
- Payment reminder email (3+ days) now carries the pay button and cancel link.

**Member cancel from email** (no sign-in)
- The cancel link is `/t/<slug>/pay/<id>?cancel=<token>` where the token is HMAC-SHA256 over `cancel:v1:tenantId:requestId:expiry` keyed with `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`, 30 day TTL, timing-safe compare. No migration, no new secret. Rotating the session secret invalidates outstanding cancel links.
- `POST requests/[id]/cancel-by-token` cancels from SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT / AWAITING_EXEMPTION_REVIEW, idempotent, and refuses if Stripe shows a payment succeeded or processing (even when `paidAt` is still null because the webhook is late).
- The pay page shows a "Cancel this request" form only when the token is present, strips the token from the address bar after reading it, and shows a cancelled card afterwards.

**Stripe hygiene**
- Leaving the money-owed states (cancel, reject, exemption granted) with a live intent: ask Stripe first. `processing` blocks the transition; `succeeded` records `paidAt` so cancel/reject auto-refund as before; otherwise the intent is voided so an old emailed link cannot charge.
- `payment-info` only hands out a client secret in SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT and reports cancelled / rejected explicitly.
- A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change gets a fresh intent; the superseded one is voided.

- `payment-exempt` now accepts SUBMITTED (the UI already offered the button; the route rejected it). Orphans refused.

---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-paidat-is-a-cache
description: AccessBuddy fobRequests.paidAt lags Stripe; any action that demands or forgives money must read the PaymentIntent from Stripe first
metadata:
  type: project
---

In AccessBuddy, `fobRequests.paidAt` is set only by the `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook, so a late or failed webhook leaves a paid request looking unpaid. The money-owed states are SUBMITTED and AWAITING_PAYMENT; priced member requests rest in SUBMITTED until the member pays or asks for an exemption (the client payment step makes no API call).

**Why:** PR #104 (merged 14 Oct 2026) added Require Payment, Resend Payment Link, a nightly abandoned-payment sweep and a signed cancel link. Both the advisor and the code-review agent independently flagged that keying any of those off `paidAt` could email "please pay" to someone who had paid, or cancel a paid request with no refund.

**How to apply:** before any new action that demands, resends, forgives or cancels payment, call `retrievePaymentIntent` (apps/web/src/lib/stripe.ts) and branch on `succeeded` / `processing`; `ensurePaymentIntent` and `requestHasPaymentInFlight` in `lib/services/requests.ts` already do this and should be reused. A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change needs a fresh intent, and the old one should be voided. The cancel link token is HMAC over `cancel:v1:tenantId:requestId:expiry` with `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`; rotating that secret invalidates outstanding cancel links. See [[gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access]] for how PRs are opened and merged from the Mac.

content.text:
═══ PAI ═══════════════════════════
🔄 ITERATION on: v1.19.0 shipped Require Payment from Submitted and Awaiting Approval only; you're asking about closed requests.

📃 CONTENT:

**No, not today.** Issued is a terminal state in the state machine, so no transition leaves it, and Require Payment only appears while a request is Submitted or Awaiting Approval. On those two states the button does show on exempt requests (that was deliberate, to override an exemption granted in error). On an issued request it is absent entirely, exempt or not.

**Your proposal works and is the right shape.** Require Payment from Issued moves it to Awaiting Payment, and payment received returns it to Issued rather than Awaiting Approval. The mechanism already exists: Hold/Resume stores the previous status on the row and resumes to it. The same pattern handles this, so it is a modest change, not a redesign.

**Four wrinkles the build has to cover,** because Awaiting Payment currently assumes the request is pre-approval:
- Payment received must route back to Issued, and send the "payment confirmed" email rather than the "request received" one.
- The cancel link in the payment email must not exist for a post-issue demand. Cancelling would cancel a request whose fob is already in the member's hand. The email would carry only Pay Now, and cancel-by-token would refuse these.
- Grant Exemption from that state must also return to Issued, not Awaiting Approval.
- The credential stays active throughout. If you want non-payment to have teeth, that is a separate decision (deactivate after N days unpaid), and I would not bundle it.

Cancelled and Rejected requests I would leave alone; Reopen already exists for those and puts them back through approval.

🗣️ Jarvis: Not possible yet; Issued is terminal. Your return-to-Issued design is sound and cheap to add.

task: "Require payment on issued requests, return to issued, withdraw action"
slug: 20261016-accessbuddy-require-payment-on-issued
project: accessbuddy
effort: advanced
effort_source: classifier
phase: build
progress: 0/34
mode: interactive

updated: 2026-10-16T09:00:00+11:00
---

## Problem

Issued is terminal, so a club cannot demand payment on a credential that was issued free (exempt by category, exemption granted in error). Nick wants Require Payment on issued requests, with payment or a withdrawn demand returning the request to Issued rather than re-entering approval.

## Vision

An approver opens an issued, unpaid request and clicks Require Payment. The member is emailed a pay link (no cancel link, the fob is in their hand). When they pay, the request is Issued again with paidAt set. If the club changes its mind, Withdraw Payment Request puts it straight back to Issued and voids the Stripe intent.

## Out of Scope

Deactivating the credential on non-payment. Require Payment on Cancelled or Rejected (Reopen covers those). Member-side decline of a post-issue demand.

## Constraints

- Return target stored on the row (`payment_return_status`), hand-written SQL migration plus journal entry, matching 0017's pattern; CI applies all migrations from zero and runs the drift check.
- No change to webhook signature handling.
- Branch from origin/main (v1.20.0); PR for Nick to merge.

## Goal

PR on `feat/require-payment-on-issued` where PAYMENT_REQUIRED is valid from ISSUED, every exit from the resulting Awaiting Payment returns to ISSUED, a WITHDRAW_PAYMENT_REQUEST admin action exists, no cancel path reaches a post-issue demand, typecheck and tests green.

## Criteria

- [ ] ISC-1: schema has paymentReturnStatus text column on fobRequests
- [ ] ISC-2: migration 0018 adds payment_return_status and journal has idx 18
- [ ] ISC-3: state machine ISSUED allows PAYMENT_REQUIRED (no longer type final)
- [ ] ISC-4: state machine AWAITING_PAYMENT allows WITHDRAW_PAYMENT_REQUEST
- [ ] ISC-5: resolveNewStatus maps ISSUED+PAYMENT_REQUIRED and AWAITING_PAYMENT+WITHDRAW
- [ ] ISC-6: PAYMENT_REQUIRED from ISSUED stores paymentReturnStatus=issued
- [ ] ISC-7: PAYMENT_RECEIVED with return status set lands on ISSUED and clears it
- [ ] ISC-8: PAYMENT_EXEMPT with return status lands on ISSUED and clears it
- [ ] ISC-9: APPROVE_EXEMPTION with return status lands on ISSUED and clears it
- [ ] ISC-10: WITHDRAW_PAYMENT_REQUEST lands on ISSUED, clears it, restores paymentExempt=true
- [ ] ISC-11: WITHDRAW without return status throws a Cannot error
- [ ] ISC-12: CANCEL with return status set throws (withdraw instead)
- [ ] ISC-13: WITHDRAW voids the Stripe intent via the leaves-payment block; succeeded blocks it
- [ ] ISC-14: audit entry toState is the actual return status
- [ ] ISC-15: admin notification skipped when returning to ISSUED
- [ ] ISC-16: member PAYMENT_RECEIVED email uses paymentReceived template when returning
- [ ] ISC-17: paymentRequired email omits cancel link for post-issue demands
- [ ] ISC-18: new payment_request_withdrawn email event and template sent on WITHDRAW
- [ ] ISC-19: resend-payment-link omits cancel link when return status set
- [ ] ISC-20: cron reminder omits cancel link when return status set
- [ ] ISC-21: cancel-by-token refuses when return status set
- [ ] ISC-22: payment-required route accepts ISSUED
- [ ] ISC-23: new route withdraw-payment-request, APPROVE_EXEMPTION, optional reason
- [ ] ISC-24: admin UI Require Payment visible on issued unpaid requests
- [ ] ISC-25: admin UI Withdraw Payment Request visible only when return status set
- [ ] ISC-26: admin UI hides Cancel and Grant Exemption when return status set
- [ ] ISC-27: page passes paymentReturnStatus to AdminActions
- [ ] ISC-28: audit labels for issued_awaiting_payment, awaiting_payment_issued, exemption return, withdraw
- [ ] ISC-29: FLOWS.md rows for the new transitions
- [ ] ISC-30: shared state-machine tests cover issued->awaiting_payment->withdraw and ->payment
- [ ] ISC-31: tests asserting ISSUED is final updated in three files
- [ ] ISC-32: typecheck, lint, tests green
- [ ] ISC-33: Anti: no webhook signature or Stripe account changes
- [ ] ISC-34: Anti: cron sweep still only touches SUBMITTED

## Test Strategy

| isc | type | check | tool |
|-----|------|-------|------|
| 1-2 | file | schema + sql + journal | Read |
| 3-5, 30-31 | unit | vitest shared + web | bun test |
| 6-23 | code | Read hunks | Read |
| 24-29 | code | Read tsx/md | Read |
| 32 | build | turbo typecheck/lint/test | Bash |
| 33-34 | git | diff --stat | Bash |

## Features

| name | satisfies | depends_on | parallelizable |
|------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| schema-migration | 1-2 | none | yes |
| state-machine | 3-5, 30-31 | none | yes |
| transition-core | 6-16 | schema, state-machine | no |
| emails | 17-20 | transition-core | no |
| routes | 21-23 | transition-core | no |
| admin-ui | 24-29 | routes | no |

## Decisions

- 2026-10-16: Return target is a dedicated column, not holdPreviousStatus, because HOLD from Awaiting Payment would clobber it.
- 2026-10-16: Withdraw restores paymentExempt=true; a post-issue demand can only exist on a request that was free, since paid ones hide the button.
- 2026-10-16: Grant Exemption hidden on post-issue demands; Withdraw is the same outcome with clearer wording.

## Problem

Issued is terminal, so a club cannot demand payment on a credential that was issued free (exempt by category, exemption granted in error). Nick wants Require Payment on issued requests, with payment or a withdrawn demand returning the request to Issued rather than re-entering approval.

## Vision

An approver opens an issued, unpaid request and clicks Require Payment. The member is emailed a pay link (no cancel link, the fob is in their hand). When they pay, the request is Issued again with paidAt set. If the club changes its mind, Withdraw Payment Request puts it straight back to Issued and voids the Stripe intent.

## Out of Scope

Deactivating the credential on non-payment. Require Payment on Cancelled or Rejected (Reopen covers those). Member-side decline of a post-issue demand.

## Constraints

- Return target stored on the row (`payment_return_status`), hand-written SQL migration plus journal entry, matching 0017's pattern; CI applies all migrations from zero and runs the drift check.
- No change to webhook signature handling.

import {
  pgTable,
  uuid,
  text,
  boolean,
  integer,
  timestamp,
  index,
} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { RequestStatus, RequestType, CredentialStatus } from "@accessbuddy/shared";
import { tenants } from "./tenants";
import { users } from "./users";
import { credentialTypes, accessLevels, pickupLocations } from "./credentials";

export const fobRequests = pgTable("fob_requests", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  tenantId: uuid("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  requesterId: uuid("requester_id")
    .references(() => users.id),
  credentialTypeId: uuid("credential_type_id")
    .references(() => credentialTypes.id),
  accessLevelId: uuid("access_level_id").references(() => accessLevels.id),
  pickupLocationId: uuid("pickup_location_id").references(
    () => pickupLocations.id
  ),
  status: text("status").notNull().default(RequestStatus.SUBMITTED),
  requestType: text("request_type").notNull().default(RequestType.NEW),
  replacesCredentialId: uuid("replaces_credential_id"),
  paymentExempt: boolean("payment_exempt").notNull().default(false),
  paymentAmountCents: integer("payment_amount_cents"),
  stripePaymentIntentId: text("stripe_payment_intent_id"),
  isOrphaned: boolean("is_orphaned").notNull().default(false),
  orphanEmail: text("orphan_email"),
  orphanFirstName: text("orphan_first_name"),
  orphanLastName: text("orphan_last_name"),
  orphanDateOfBirth: text("orphan_date_of_birth"),
  relatedRequestId: uuid("related_request_id"),
  membershipCategory: text("membership_category"),
  credentialExpiresAt: timestamp("credential_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  accessUpdateReason: text("access_update_reason"),
  // Payment exemption fields
  exemptionRequested: boolean("exemption_requested").notNull().default(false),
  exemptionReason: text("exemption_reason"),
  exemptionReviewedBy: uuid("exemption_reviewed_by").references(() => users.id),
  exemptionReviewedAt: timestamp("exemption_reviewed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  exemptionApproved: boolean("exemption_approved"),
  exemptionRejectionReason: text("exemption_rejection_reason"),
  // Refund fields
  refundedAt: timestamp("refunded_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  refundedBy: uuid("refunded_by").references(() => users.id),
  refundReason: text("refund_reason"),
  stripeRefundId: text("stripe_refund_id"),
  holdReason: text("hold_reason"),
  holdPreviousStatus: text("hold_previous_status"),
  cancelReason: text("cancel_reason"),
  cancelledBy: uuid("cancelled_by").references(() => users.id),
  submittedAt: timestamp("submitted_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  paidAt: timestamp("paid_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  approvedAt: timestamp("approved_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  approvedBy: uuid("approved_by").references(() => users.id),
  programmedAt: timestamp("programmed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  programmedBy: uuid("programmed_by").references(() => users.id),
  issuedAt: timestamp("issued_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  issuedBy: uuid("issued_by").references(() => users.id),
  // Set only when the daily cron closes a return whose fob was never handed in.
  autoClosedAt: timestamp("auto_closed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  serialNumber: text("serial_number"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
}, (table) => [
  // Admin queue filters by tenant + status; no secondary index existed
  // (FKs do not create indexes in Postgres), forcing a sequential scan.
  index("fob_requests_tenant_status_idx").on(table.tenantId, table.status),
  // Dispute webhook looks up the request by payment intent id.
  index("fob_requests_stripe_payment_intent_idx").on(table.stripePaymentIntentId),
  // Request lifecycle / member views look up a user's own requests.
  index("fob_requests_requester_idx").on(table.requesterId),
]);

export const credentials = pgTable("credentials", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  tenantId: uuid("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  ownerId: uuid("owner_id")
    .references(() => users.id),
  credentialTypeId: uuid("credential_type_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => credentialTypes.id),
  accessLevelId: uuid("access_level_id")
    .references(() => accessLevels.id),
  requestId: uuid("request_id")
    .references(() => fobRequests.id),
  serialNumber: text("serial_number"),
  externalCardId: text("external_card_id"),
  status: text("status").notNull().default(CredentialStatus.ACTIVE),
  issuedAt: timestamp("issued_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
  accessStartsAt: timestamp("access_starts_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  deactivatedAt: timestamp("deactivated_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  deactivatedBy: uuid("deactivated_by").references(() => users.id),
  deactivationReason: text("deactivation_reason"),
  lostReportedAt: timestamp("lost_reported_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  programmingRequired: boolean("programming_required").notNull().default(false),
  programmingReason: text("programming_reason"),
  programmingRequestedAt: timestamp("programming_requested_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  pendingExpiresAt: timestamp("pending_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
}, (table) => [
  // Admin queue and cron filter credentials by tenant + status.
  index("credentials_tenant_status_idx").on(table.tenantId, table.status),
  // Member/owner lookups (dashboard, cron sweep) by owner.
  index("credentials_owner_idx").on(table.ownerId),
  // Request lifecycle joins a credential back to its originating request.
  index("credentials_request_idx").on(table.requestId),
  // Serial-number lookup (programming, lost/found, reconciliation).
  index("credentials_serial_number_idx").on(table.serialNumber),
]);

content.content:
The design is sound, but there are two gaps I'd treat as blocking, plus several risks to check before you open the PR.

**Blocking**

1. **Moving an issued fob out of ISSUED may deactivate it without anyone deciding to.** Deactivation is out of scope, but any code that treats `status = 'issued'` as "this fob is live" will now drop the fob while payment is owed. Grep every `ISSUED` / `eq(status, 'issued')` across reports, CSV exports, credential registry views, member counts, and the PR #106 return/change_type retirement paths. If any of them feed access lists or "active credential" counts, a payment demand quietly turns the fob off. Either make those checks also accept `paymentReturnStatus = 'issued'`, or state in the PR that this is intended. The member dashboard problem you listed is the visible part of this same issue.
2. **A stale return status can send a later request straight to ISSUED.** The column must only be acted on when the current status is AWAITING_PAYMENT, or the exemption sub-states reached from it. It must also be cleared on every exit, not just the ones that land on ISSUED. Two paths to check:
   - **Admin exits.** Can REJECT, a HOLD→cancel chain, or Reopen move the request somewhere other than ISSUED while the column is still set? If so, a later PAYMENT_RECEIVED jumps straight to ISSUED and skips approval.
   - **Member exemption requests.** If a member can ask for an exemption from AWAITING_PAYMENT, REJECT_EXEMPTION must return to AWAITING_PAYMENT with the column kept. CANCEL from the exemption-requested state must also be refused while the column is set.

   Add a guard of the form "override only if the current status is in {AWAITING_PAYMENT, the exemption-requested states}". Also add an assertion that the column is null whenever the status is not one of those.

**High-risk, check these**

3. **The awaiting-payment sweep from PR #104.** ISC-34 covers the SUBMITTED sweep. But if PR #104 added an auto-cancel or expiry sweep for stale AWAITING_PAYMENT rows, your new CANCEL refusal will throw inside the cron. That can break the batch or retry every run. Filter `payment_return_status IS NULL` in the sweep query itself rather than relying on the throw.
4. **The webhook path.** Confirm every `payment_intent.succeeded` handler goes through `transitionRequest` and gets the override. Watch for direct `UPDATE`s or a separate "mark paid" helper. Also consider this race: withdraw voids the intent, then a late succeeded or processing webhook arrives for a request that is already ISSUED. PAYMENT_RECEIVED from ISSUED is now invalid. Make sure that case is a logged no-op (returns 200), not a throw that Stripe retries for 3 days. Per the paidAt-is-a-cache memory, also check that reading the intent reports a succeeded-after-withdraw intent rather than hiding it.
5. **Restoring `paymentExempt=true` on withdraw assumes too much.** Your argument is that the button only shows on free requests. "Unpaid" (`paidAt` null) is not the same as "was exempt". Older rows, or rows approved without payment while `paymentExempt=false`, would be flipped to exempt by a withdraw. Safer: snapshot the prior `paymentExempt` when the demand is made, or show the button only when `paymentExempt=true`, not merely when unpaid.
6. **Concurrency.** Withdraw and the webhook can run at the same moment. Make sure the status update is guarded (`WHERE status = 'awaiting_payment'`, or a row lock) so only one of them wins.

**Smaller items**

- Audit labels for the new withdraw action need adding in both renderers (from PR #102).
- The drift check: if it compares against a drizzle snapshot, make sure 0018 matches it the way 0017 does. If `accessbuddy_app` has column-level grants anywhere, add a grant for the new column.
- Tests: your test strategy checks ISC-6 to 16 by reading the code. That logic is where the bugs will be. Add unit or integration tests for the override and clearing, and for refused CANCEL and WITHDRAW, if the harness allows it.
- Member dashboard: don't leave it untouched. Either do a cheap fix, such as showing a "Payment requested" badge and the issued fob when the column is set, or list it explicitly as a known gap in the PR description.
- For deploying after merge, remember the release-race gotcha (rerun with `--failed`).

Fix items 1 and 2 (or decide on item 1 and document it) before the PR. Items 3 to 6 are quick checks that could each turn into a production bug.

content.content:
The design is sound, but there are two gaps I'd treat as blocking, plus several risks to check before you open the PR.

**Blocking**

1. **Moving an issued fob out of ISSUED may deactivate it without anyone deciding to.** Deactivation is out of scope, but any code that treats `status = 'issued'` as "this fob is live" will now drop the fob while payment is owed. Grep every `ISSUED` / `eq(status, 'issued')` across reports, CSV exports, credential registry views, member counts, and the PR #106 return/change_type retirement paths. If any of them feed access lists or "active credential" counts, a payment demand quietly turns the fob off. Either make those checks also accept `paymentReturnStatus = 'issued'`, or state in the PR that this is intended. The member dashboard problem you listed is the visible part of this same issue.
2. **A stale return status can send a later request straight to ISSUED.** The column must only be acted on when the current status is AWAITING_PAYMENT, or the exemption sub-states reached from it. It must also be cleared on every exit, not just the ones that land on ISSUED. Two paths to check:
   - **Admin exits.** Can REJECT, a HOLD→cancel chain, or Reopen move the request somewhere other than ISSUED while the column is still set? If so, a later PAYMENT_RECEIVED jumps straight to ISSUED and skips approval.
   - **Member exemption requests.** If a member can ask for an exemption from AWAITING_PAYMENT, REJECT_EXEMPTION must return to AWAITING_PAYMENT with the column kept. CANCEL from the exemption-requested state must also be refused while the column is set.

   Add a guard of the form "override only if the current status is in {AWAITING_PAYMENT, the exemption-requested states}". Also add an assertion that the column is null whenever the status is not one of those.

**High-risk, check these**

3. **The awaiting-payment sweep from PR #104.** ISC-34 covers the SUBMITTED sweep. But if PR #104 added an auto-cancel or expiry sweep for stale AWAITING_PAYMENT rows, your new CANCEL refusal will throw inside the cron. That can break the batch or retry every run. Filter `payment_return_status IS NULL` in the sweep query itself rather than relying on the throw.
4. **The webhook path.** Confirm every `payment_intent.succeeded` handler goes through `transitionRequest` and gets the override. Watch for direct `UPDATE`s or a separate "mark paid" helper. Also consider this race: withdraw voids the intent, then a late succeeded or processing webhook arrives for a request that is already ISSUED. PAYMENT_RECEIVED from ISSUED is now invalid. Make sure that case is a logged no-op (returns 200), not a throw that Stripe retries for 3 days. Per the paidAt-is-a-cache memory, also check that reading the intent reports a succeeded-after-withdraw intent rather than hiding it.
5. **Restoring `paymentExempt=true` on withdraw assumes too much.** Your argument is that the button only shows on free requests. "Unpaid" (`paidAt` null) is not the same as "was exempt". Older rows, or rows approved without payment while `paymentExempt=false`, would be flipped to exempt by a withdraw. Safer: snapshot the prior `paymentExempt` when the demand is made, or show the button only when `paymentExempt=true`, not merely when unpaid.
6. **Concurrency.** Withdraw and the webhook can run at the same moment. Make sure the status update is guarded (`WHERE status = 'awaiting_payment'`, or a row lock) so only one of them wins.

**Smaller items**

- Audit labels for the new withdraw action need adding in both renderers (from PR #102).
- The drift check: if it compares against a drizzle snapshot, make sure 0018 matches it the way 0017 does. If `accessbuddy_app` has column-level grants anywhere, add a grant for the new column.
- Tests: your test strategy checks ISC-6 to 16 by reading the code. That logic is where the bugs will be. Add unit or integration tests for the override and clearing, and for refused CANCEL and WITHDRAW, if the harness allows it.
- Member dashboard: don't leave it untouched. Either do a cheap fix, such as showing a "Payment requested" badge and the issued fob when the column is set, or list it explicitly as a known gap in the PR description.
- For deploying after merge, remember the release-race gotcha (rerun with `--failed`).

Fix items 1 and 2 (or decide on item 1 and document it) before the PR. Items 3 to 6 are quick checks that could each turn into a production bug.

import {
  pgTable,
  uuid,
  text,
  boolean,
  integer,
  timestamp,
  index,
} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import { RequestStatus, RequestType, CredentialStatus } from "@accessbuddy/shared";
import { tenants } from "./tenants";
import { users } from "./users";
import { credentialTypes, accessLevels, pickupLocations } from "./credentials";

export const fobRequests = pgTable("fob_requests", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  tenantId: uuid("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  requesterId: uuid("requester_id")
    .references(() => users.id),
  credentialTypeId: uuid("credential_type_id")
    .references(() => credentialTypes.id),
  accessLevelId: uuid("access_level_id").references(() => accessLevels.id),
  pickupLocationId: uuid("pickup_location_id").references(
    () => pickupLocations.id
  ),
  status: text("status").notNull().default(RequestStatus.SUBMITTED),
  requestType: text("request_type").notNull().default(RequestType.NEW),
  replacesCredentialId: uuid("replaces_credential_id"),
  paymentExempt: boolean("payment_exempt").notNull().default(false),
  paymentAmountCents: integer("payment_amount_cents"),
  stripePaymentIntentId: text("stripe_payment_intent_id"),
  isOrphaned: boolean("is_orphaned").notNull().default(false),
  orphanEmail: text("orphan_email"),
  orphanFirstName: text("orphan_first_name"),
  orphanLastName: text("orphan_last_name"),
  orphanDateOfBirth: text("orphan_date_of_birth"),
  relatedRequestId: uuid("related_request_id"),
  membershipCategory: text("membership_category"),
  credentialExpiresAt: timestamp("credential_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  accessUpdateReason: text("access_update_reason"),
  // Payment exemption fields
  exemptionRequested: boolean("exemption_requested").notNull().default(false),
  exemptionReason: text("exemption_reason"),
  exemptionReviewedBy: uuid("exemption_reviewed_by").references(() => users.id),
  exemptionReviewedAt: timestamp("exemption_reviewed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  exemptionApproved: boolean("exemption_approved"),
  exemptionRejectionReason: text("exemption_rejection_reason"),
  // Refund fields
  refundedAt: timestamp("refunded_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  refundedBy: uuid("refunded_by").references(() => users.id),
  refundReason: text("refund_reason"),
  stripeRefundId: text("stripe_refund_id"),
  holdReason: text("hold_reason"),
  holdPreviousStatus: text("hold_previous_status"),
  // Set when payment is required on an already-issued request. Holds the
  // status to return to ("issued") once paid, exempted, or withdrawn, so the
  // request does not re-enter the approval queue. NULL otherwise.
  paymentReturnStatus: text("payment_return_status"),
  cancelReason: text("cancel_reason"),
  cancelledBy: uuid("cancelled_by").references(() => users.id),
  submittedAt: timestamp("submitted_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  paidAt: timestamp("paid_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  approvedAt: timestamp("approved_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  approvedBy: uuid("approved_by").references(() => users.id),
  programmedAt: timestamp("programmed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  programmedBy: uuid("programmed_by").references(() => users.id),
  issuedAt: timestamp("issued_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  issuedBy: uuid("issued_by").references(() => users.id),
  // Set only when the daily cron closes a return whose fob was never handed in.
  autoClosedAt: timestamp("auto_closed_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  serialNumber: text("serial_number"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
}, (table) => [
  // Admin queue filters by tenant + status; no secondary index existed
  // (FKs do not create indexes in Postgres), forcing a sequential scan.
  index("fob_requests_tenant_status_idx").on(table.tenantId, table.status),
  // Dispute webhook looks up the request by payment intent id.
  index("fob_requests_stripe_payment_intent_idx").on(table.stripePaymentIntentId),
  // Request lifecycle / member views look up a user's own requests.
  index("fob_requests_requester_idx").on(table.requesterId),
]);

export const credentials = pgTable("credentials", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  tenantId: uuid("tenant_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => tenants.id),
  ownerId: uuid("owner_id")
    .references(() => users.id),
  credentialTypeId: uuid("credential_type_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => credentialTypes.id),
  accessLevelId: uuid("access_level_id")
    .references(() => accessLevels.id),
  requestId: uuid("request_id")
    .references(() => fobRequests.id),
  serialNumber: text("serial_number"),
  externalCardId: text("external_card_id"),
  status: text("status").notNull().default(CredentialStatus.ACTIVE),
  issuedAt: timestamp("issued_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull(),
  accessStartsAt: timestamp("access_starts_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  expiresAt: timestamp("expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  deactivatedAt: timestamp("deactivated_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  deactivatedBy: uuid("deactivated_by").references(() => users.id),
  deactivationReason: text("deactivation_reason"),
  lostReportedAt: timestamp("lost_reported_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  programmingRequired: boolean("programming_required").notNull().default(false),
  programmingReason: text("programming_reason"),
  programmingRequestedAt: timestamp("programming_requested_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  pendingExpiresAt: timestamp("pending_expires_at", { withTimezone: true }),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at", { withTimezone: true })
    .notNull()
    .defaultNow(),
}, (table) => [
  // Admin queue and cron filter credentials by tenant + status.
  index("credentials_tenant_status_idx").on(table.tenantId, table.status),
  // Member/owner lookups (dashboard, cron sweep) by owner.
  index("credentials_owner_idx").on(table.ownerId),
  // Request lifecycle joins a credential back to its originating request.
  index("credentials_request_idx").on(table.requestId),
  // Serial-number lookup (programming, lost/found, reconciliation).
  index("credentials_serial_number_idx").on(table.serialNumber),
]);

-- Set when an admin requires payment on a request that was already issued
-- (for example a credential issued free under an exemption granted in error).
-- payment_return_status holds the status to return to ("issued") once payment
-- is received, an exemption is granted, or the payment request is withdrawn,
-- so the request does not re-enter the approval queue. payment_return_exempt
-- snapshots payment_exempt at the time of the demand so a withdrawal restores
-- the prior flag. Both NULL for every ordinary request.
ALTER TABLE "fob_requests" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "payment_return_status" text;
ALTER TABLE "fob_requests" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "payment_return_exempt" boolean;

<result>Nothing here blocks the merge. The core design holds up: what gets written to the database and to Stripe is correct for every path you asked me to check. I found two important issues and three lower-severity problems with emails, copy and controls.

I reviewed commit `162d52c` (20 files) against the project brief at `/home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/CLAUDE.md`. There is no CLAUDE.md inside `code/`. Its hard rules are about infra and access levels, and none of them are touched. Shared tests (26) and web tests (237) pass, and `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/web` is clean.

## Important

**1. Require Payment is offered on any issued request, including returns, access updates and change-type requests (confidence 85)**
- **Where:** `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/requests/[id]/payment-required/route.ts:16-20` and `admin-actions.tsx:147-148`.
- **Cause:** Neither checks the request type. `ensurePaymentIntent` (`requests.ts:2229-2242`) charges the price of whatever `credentialTypeId` is on the request.
- **Failure:** An admin opens an issued RETURN (the member has already handed the fob back) and clicks Require Payment. The member gets a bill for the full fob price. The email says "Your credential stays active", which is false for a returned or deactivated fob.
- **Fix:** For `current.status === ISSUED`, require `PAYMENT_REQUIRED_REQUEST_TYPES.includes(current.requestType)` in the route, and apply the same check to `canRequirePayment` in the UI.

**2. On a damaged-fob request, approving an exemption on a post-issue demand sends the request back to the programming queue (confidence 80)**
- **Where:** `requests.ts:1319-1344`.
- **Cause:** This block always moves a REPLACEMENT_DAMAGED request to AWAITING_PROGRAMMING when an exemption is approved. It runs after your override (`requests.ts:506-508`) has already set the status to ISSUED, so it undoes it.
- **Failure:** A damaged fob is issued free under an exemption, and the admin later requires payment. Someone then calls `request-exemption`. That route needs no login, but the pay page doesn't link to it, so it's a hand-built call. When the admin approves, the request goes ISSUED → AWAITING_PROGRAMMING and `approvedAt` is stamped again. The audit trail shows "→ issued" followed by "awaiting_approval → awaiting_programming". A later PROGRAM re-deactivates the old fob, sets status ISSUED with a fresh `issuedAt` (`requests.ts:1353-1361`), and emails `credentialDeactivated` again. This is exactly the case you wanted ruled out in question 2.
- **Fix:** Add `&& !request.paymentReturnStatus` to the condition at line 1319.

## Lower severity (55-75, not blocking)

3. **Damaged-fob requests get the wrong email when a post-issue demand settles.** At `requests.ts:1766-1773`, the `isDamagedInitialEvent` check runs before your new `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` branch at 1974. A damaged request paid after issue gets `damagedFobReported` instead of `paymentReceived(alreadyIssued)`. The same happens for PAYMENT_EXEMPT. Damaged fobs are the most likely real case of "issued free in error". Fix: exclude requests with `paymentReturnStatus` set from that check.

4. **The queue card still offers Grant Exemption and the copy is wrong.** `queue-item.tsx:81-83` and `:635-660` still show "Grant Exemption … send this request to approval" on a post-issue AWAITING_PAYMENT request, which the detail page now hides. The service handles it correctly (the request returns to ISSUED). But the member then gets `exemptionApproved`, which says "Your request will now be reviewed…" (`email-templates.ts:431-434`, sent from `requests.ts:2005-2010`). The same wrong email goes out for APPROVE_EXEMPTION after issue.

5. **Members see a Cancel button that always fails.** `dashboard/requests/[id]/page.tsx:79-84` shows Cancel for any status except issued, cancelled or rejected. On a post-issue demand the click hits `requests.ts:501-504`, and the member sees "…Withdraw the payment request instead", which is an admin-only action. The fob detail page has the same problem (`admin/fobs/[id]/page.tsx:30`, `CancelLinkedRequest`). Nothing breaks, because the service refuses the cancel before any side effects run, but the control should be hidden.

## Your seven questions

1. **Ordering in `transitionRequest`:** correct.
   - The audit `toState` uses `updateValues.status`, so it records ISSUED.
   - The Stripe "leaving payment" block voids the intent on WITHDRAW. It refuses when Stripe shows the payment as processing or succeeded, and the throw rolls back the status update.
   - Auto-refund only fires on CANCEL or REJECT, so it doesn't run here.
   - Credential side effects only run on PROGRAM or ISSUE, so they don't run either.
   - The CANCEL guard sits at line 501, before the code at 567+ that unallocates the fob.
   - `sendTransitionEmail` reads the row as it was before the update, so `paymentReturnStatus` and `status === ISSUED` give the right answer.
2. **No credential re-creation or second `issuedAt` stamp**, except the damaged-fob chain in finding 2.
3. **Round trips:**
   - HOLD then RESUME is fine: the hold field and `payment_return_status` are separate, and RESUME isn't in the list of events that return to ISSUED.
   - REQUEST_EXEMPTION then REJECT_EXEMPTION keeps the column and goes back to AWAITING_PAYMENT.
   - REOPEN can't happen, because neither CANCELLED nor REJECTED can be reached while the column is set.
4. **Stripe webhook:** correct. The status returns to ISSUED, `paidAt` is set, and the admin "awaiting approval" email is skipped. One thing that isn't new: if the Stripe read fails during a withdraw, the intent is not voided. A later payment then fails silently on ISSUED, and the money is kept with nothing recorded. PAYMENT_EXEMPT already has the same gap, so I've left it out of the ranking. Note that the withdraw email's line "Any earlier payment link … will no longer work" isn't guaranteed in that case.
5. **State machine vs `resolveNewStatus`:** they match. `getPrimaryAction` returns null for ISSUED, and the progress stepper shows AWAITING_PAYMENT as step 1. I found no other code that assumes ISSUED has no actions.
6. **Migration:** correct.
   - It uses `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, a nullable `text` column, the same as the schema.
   - The journal entry follows 0017 in index and timestamp.
   - The drift check's planner will produce no statements, so the gate passes.
7. **Email layer:** existing `credentialNoun` call sites are unchanged. Only the new strings hardcode "credential", which is a wording choice rather than a bug.

  payment / exemption review (never stale); payment_return_exempt snapshots
  the prior exemption flag so withdraw restores it instead of assuming true
- Require Payment after issue limited to new / additional credentials
  (returns, access updates, change of type and lost/damaged records have
  nothing to bill); enforced in the route and the admin UI

  for programming; post-issue settlements get payment-received or
  payment-no-longer-required emails, never the damaged-report / review ones
- update route and admin edit controls refuse changes during a demand;
  queue card and fob page hide quick actions / cancel on it

  issued, pay-now notice with link, no member cancel
- DB-gated service test (Stripe stubbed) covering require -> cancel refused
  -> withdraw restores, require -> payment received returns to issued, and
  withdraw refused on an ordinary unpaid request" && git push -q origin feat/require-payment-on-issued 2>&1 | tail -1; git log --oneline -3
cat > /tmp/pr-body-2.md <<'EOF'
## Why

Issued was a terminal state, so a club could not demand payment on a credential that was issued free (category exemption, or an exemption granted in error). Nick's ask: Require Payment on issued requests, with payment or a withdrawn demand returning the request to Issued rather than re-entering approval, and an admin way to cancel the payment request.

## What

**Require Payment from Issued** (`POST requests/[id]/payment-required`, same `approve_exemption` permission). Limited after issue to `new` and `additional` request types; a return, access update, change of type or lost/damaged record has nothing to bill. Creates the Stripe intent if needed and emails the member a pay link. The email has **no cancel link** (the fob is in their hand) and says the credential stays active.

**Return to Issued.** Two new nullable columns on `fob_requests` (migration 0018, hand-written like 0017): `payment_return_status` records `issued` when the demand is raised, and `payment_return_exempt` snapshots the prior exemption flag. While the request sits in Awaiting Payment (or exemption review reached from it), `PAYMENT_RECEIVED`, `PAYMENT_EXEMPT`, `APPROVE_EXEMPTION` and the new `WITHDRAW_PAYMENT_REQUEST` all land back on Issued and clear the columns. The stored status is only honoured from those two states, so it can never be stale. No admin "awaiting approval" email fires when a post-issue demand settles.

**Withdraw Payment Request** (`POST requests/[id]/withdraw-payment-request`, optional reason). Returns to Issued, restores the snapshotted exemption flag, voids the Stripe intent (refuses if Stripe shows the payment processing or succeeded), emails the member via a new `payment_request_withdrawn` event. Refused on requests that were never issued.

**Guards while a demand is outstanding.** Cancel is refused (service, admin UI, fob page, member dashboard, cancel-by-token); Grant Exemption hidden on the detail page and the queue card has no quick action; the update route and admin edit controls refuse changes; the damaged-fob exemption path no longer re-queues the request for programming.

**Member side.** Dashboard badge reads "Issued, payment requested", the stepper stays on Issued, the request page shows the amount with a Pay now link, and no cancel button.

**State machine.** `ISSUED` is no longer an xstate final state; its only event is `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`. Three tests that asserted "Issued is final" updated.

## Tests
- shared: issued only allows PAYMENT_REQUIRED; awaiting_payment allows WITHDRAW; round trips
- web: post-issue email variants; new DB-gated service test (Stripe stubbed) covering require → cancel refused → withdraw restores exemption, require → payment received returns to issued with paidAt, withdraw refused on an ordinary unpaid request (runs in CI against Postgres)
- typecheck, lint, test green locally; drift check runs in CI

## Not in scope
Deactivating the credential on non-payment. Member-side decline of a post-issue demand.

## Review
Advisor pass and an independent code-review agent pass; findings folded into the second commit (stale-status guard, exemption snapshot, billable-type restriction, damaged-fob re-queue, email routing, hidden controls).
EOF

**Return to Issued.** Two new nullable columns on `fob_requests` (migration 0018, hand-written like 0017): `payment_return_status` records `issued` when the demand is raised, and `payment_return_exempt` snapshots the prior exemption flag. While the request sits in Awaiting Payment (or exemption review reached from it), `PAYMENT_RECEIVED`, `PAYMENT_EXEMPT`, `APPROVE_EXEMPTION` and the new `WITHDRAW_PAYMENT_REQUEST` all land back on Issued and clear the columns. The stored status is only honoured from those two states, so it can never be stale. No admin "awaiting approval" email fires when a post-issue demand settles.

**Withdraw Payment Request** (`POST requests/[id]/withdraw-payment-request`, optional reason). Returns to Issued, restores the snapshotted exemption flag, voids the Stripe intent (refuses if Stripe shows the payment processing or succeeded), emails the member via a new `payment_request_withdrawn` event. Refused on requests that were never issued.

**Guards while a demand is outstanding.** Cancel is refused (service, admin UI, fob page, member dashboard, cancel-by-token); Grant Exemption hidden on the detail page and the queue card has no quick action; the update route and admin edit controls refuse changes; the damaged-fob exemption path no longer re-queues the request for programming.

**Member side.** Dashboard badge reads "Issued, payment requested", the stepper stays on Issued, the request page shows the amount with a Pay now link, and no cancel button.

**State machine.** `ISSUED` is no longer an xstate final state; its only event is `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`. Three tests that asserted "Issued is final" updated.

- shared: issued only allows PAYMENT_REQUIRED; awaiting_payment allows WITHDRAW; round trips
- web: post-issue email variants; new DB-gated service test (Stripe stubbed) covering require → cancel refused → withdraw restores exemption, require → payment received returns to issued with paidAt, withdraw refused on an ordinary unpaid request (runs in CI against Postgres)
- typecheck, lint, test green locally; drift check runs in CI

## Not in scope
Deactivating the credential on non-payment. Member-side decline of a post-issue demand.

## Review
Advisor pass and an independent code-review agent pass; findings folded into the second commit (stale-status guard, exemption snapshot, billable-type restriction, damaged-fob re-queue, email routing, hidden controls).

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: you asked for Require Payment on issued requests with payment or a withdrawn demand returning to Issued.

📃 CONTENT:

**PR #109 is open and all four checks are green: https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/109.** The Test job matters most here because it ran the new migration from zero, the schema-drift gate, and the new database-gated service test with Stripe stubbed. I have not merged it; the earlier approvals covered #104 and #105 only.

**What it does.** On an issued `new` or `additional` request an approver now sees **Require Payment**. The member is emailed a pay link with no cancel option, told the credential stays active, and the request sits in Awaiting Payment with a stored return target. Paying, granting an exemption, or the new **Withdraw Payment Request** button all land the request back on Issued. Withdraw restores whatever the exemption flag was before the demand, voids the Stripe intent, and emails the member that no payment is due.

**What is locked while a demand is outstanding.** Cancel everywhere (admin, fob page, member dashboard, the emailed link), Grant Exemption on the detail page and queue card, and edits to the request. The member's dashboard shows "Issued, payment requested" with a Pay now link.

**One restriction worth knowing.** Require Payment after issue is limited to `new` and `additional` requests. A return, access update, change of type or lost/damaged record has nothing to bill, and the reviewer showed an admin could otherwise bill the full fob price on a fob already handed back.

**Deploy path is the same as last time.** Merge #109, release-please opens the release PR, merge that to ship. The migration runs at container start.

🖊️ STORY:
- Issued was terminal, so free credentials could not be billed
- Added return-to-issued demand, withdraw action, guards everywhere
- Two reviews caught billing returns and a damaged-fob re-queue
- PR 109 green; merge when ready

════ PAI | NATIVE MODE ═══════════════════════
🗒️ TASK: Point to the Require Payment button location
🔄 ITERATION on: PR #109 merged into v1.21.0, which another session shipped later on 18 Oct, so the button is live.

📃 CONTENT:

Open any request's detail page in the admin area, `/t/smlsc/admin/requests/<request id>`, and look in the **Actions** card. The button is labelled **Require Payment**, next to Grant Exemption, and a reason box opens when you click it. It is not on the queue cards, only on the detail page.

It only appears when all of these hold:
- The request is **Submitted**, **Awaiting Approval**, or **Issued**. On an issued request it is further limited to `new` and `additional` request types, so you will not see it on an issued return, access update, change of type, or lost/damaged record.
- Nothing has been paid (`paidAt` empty). A paid request shows Refund Payment instead.
- The request is not orphaned. Link it to a member first.
- You hold the **approve_exemption** permission, the same one that gates Grant Exemption.

If a request meets all four and you still do not see it, tell me which request and I will check it on the live site.

🔧 CHANGE: None.
✅ VERIFY: Button logic read from admin-actions.tsx; v1.21.0 live per the later release.
🗣️ Jarvis: Request detail page, Actions card, labelled Require Payment, on unpaid new or additional requests.
